newsitem.title: UK: Change at top of Cubazucar surprises traders.
newsitem.headline: Change at top of Cubazucar surprises traders.

text.p: London sugar traders expressed surprise at reports that Cuba is changing the president of its state sugar trading firm, Cubazucar, but doubted if the move would have much longer term impact on the market.
"Surprise, I think, is the general reaction. Everyone's wondering why," said a trader with a major London house involved with Cuba.
Industry sources have said that Alberto Betancourt, long-time Cubazucar head and a respected figure on international sugar markets, was removed from his post on December 24.
No official reason has yet emerged, nor has there been any mention of the change in Cuba's state-run media.

William Parra, a former deputy president of Cubazucar, is reported to be acting as its temporary president. "The decision was taken without consultation with central authorities and there are various hypotheses about what it might exactly mean -- but that's the only thing official so far," said another trader.
"We certainly weren't expecting him (Betancourt) to be dismissed. Whether Parra remains in charge permanently remains to be seen," said a third.
Market sources in London said the move was unlikely to have any significant impact on world markets or on Cuba's long-term commitments to supply sugar from its 1996/97 harvest.
